gaps.title: Mélodie arabe, Op. 4 No. 4 (arr. Kochański)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (arrangement of the 4th of the 5 Romances for voice and piano, Op. 4, also known as 'Arabian Melody'; Glazunov's own cello version exists too)
gaps.edition: Paul Kochanski arr., A.E. Fischer, New York 1933 (plate 22628); also Schott ED 7354 'Mélodie arabe' for violin & piano ed./arr. Samuel Dushkin (in 'Samuel Dushkin Repertoire', ED 20423); J. & W. Chester edition 'for cello or violin and piano' (J.W.C. 901)
gaps.note: Second source: Boosey & Hawkes shop lists the Schott ED 7354 violin & piano edition (Dushkin) https://www.boosey.com/shop/prod/Glazunov-Alexander-Melodie-Arabe-violin-piano/2156444 . Recording evidence: Kochanski made Brunswick matrices 725W-727W 'Melodie arabe' with Gregory Ashman in 1925 (DAHR, unissued/unknown status); modern commercial recordings are mostly cello. Pick Kochanski as the arranger credit (IMSLP) or Dushkin (Schott).

gaps.title: Valse (from Raymonda, Op. 57) (arr. Pogojeff)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (transcription of the Act I waltz from the ballet)
gaps.edition: M.P. Belaieff BEL 808 'Two Pieces from the ballet Raymonda' (Grand Adagio + Valse, transcr. W. Pogojeff), now Schott; IMSLP also lists Pogozhev's violin & piano Waltz, Muzgiz 1950 (plate 20776)
gaps.note: OPTIONAL / LOW PRIORITY: published and in print, but I found no recording evidence and Pogojeff is not a notable performer-arranger. Add only together with the Grand Adagio (id 963) if that entry is attributed to the Pogojeff set.

existing_issues.issue: Key missing; IMSLP gives D major, 1917, dedicated to Kochanski, and lists NO opus number (Wikipedia's work list shows 'Op. 100A/B' but Op. 100 is the Piano Concerto No. 2 on IMSLP, so leave the opus out).

Title lacks the opus number and arranger ('arr.' alone). Zimbalist's violin & piano arrangement of the Raymonda Grand Adagio is published by G. Schirmer (c. 4 min); a separate Belaieff transcription by Pogojeff (BEL 808) also exists, and Heifetz recorded a 'Grand adagio' for Victor in 1922. The Raymonda ballet is Op. 57.

No change needed, but note: Albumblatt is originally for trumpet and piano (1899, D-flat major, no opus, IAG 117, ded. A. W. Kosmakov); the violin version is a Belaieff transcription by Jean-Francois Gonzales (ed. Michael/Mikhail Goldstein), SKU BEL508A, 6 pp. Retailers disagree on who is 'editor' and who is 'arranger'.
